attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden onset of weakness and pallor

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with HbSS sickle cell anemia and functional asplenia presents to the emergency department for evaluation following stable routine follow-up in January 2020. His parents report that he has been unusually fatigued and less playful over the past day.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Sickle cell anemia without crisis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Sickle cell anemia (HbSS genotype)
- Functional asplenia

His past medical history is significant for sickle cell disease.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Penicillin V potassium 125 mg orally twice daily
- Folic acid 1 mg orally daily
- Hydroxyurea 20 mg/kg orally daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Sickle cell trait (HbAS)
- Mother: Sickle cell trait (HbAS)
- Older sister: Sickle cell disease (HbSS)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
Heart rate of 130 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears lethargic
His skin is noticeably pale, and he has scleral icterus. Abdominal examination reveals a palpable mass on the left side below the costal margin.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory tests are as follows:

- Hemoglobin: 6.2 g/dL (Normal: 11-13 g/dL)
- Hematocrit: 18.5% (Normal: 34-40%)
- Reticulocyte count: 10% (Normal: 0.5-1.5%)
- Platelet count: 80,000/mm³ (Normal: 150,000-400,000/mm³)
- White blood cell count: 12,000/mm³ (Normal: 5,000-10,000/mm³)
